key: Trust is a key factor in any successful partnership.
writers: people who write books, articles or other texts
A CDC researcher was one of the study's writers.
creative: involving original ideas and imagination to produce something new
The team took a creative approach to solving the shipping delay.
should: used to say what is correct, expected, or advisable
You should see a doctor if the pain continues for another week.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum
The car will run for a while even after the engine dies.
rat: a small rodent, used here in the phrase 'rat race' for a stressful routine
He quit his job to escape the exhausting rat race.
race: a competition to see who is fastest
Thousands of runners took part in the city marathon race.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
keep: to continue having or doing something; to maintain
Please keep this document safe until the meeting next week.
soulful: The singer's soulful voice moved the entire audience to tears.
alive: Despite the harsh winter, the old tree remained alive.
judge: to form an opinion about something after careful thought
Coaches judge a player's potential by watching how they train.
reality: the way things actually are, as opposed to how they seem
The film's glamorous version of war has little to do with reality.
show: to prove or make clear that something is true
The results show that the new treatment is more effective.
called: named or referred to by a particular term
The recipe uses a fermented paste called miso for extra flavour.
idol: a person greatly admired, or an object of worship
The young singer became an idol for millions of fans.
junior: cấp dưới, con thứ hai cùng tên
She was promoted from a junior role within just two years.
notice: to become aware of something; to see or observe
I didn't notice the mistake until I read the page again.
popularity: the state of being liked or supported by many people
sự nổi tiếng, mức độ phổ biến
The singer's popularity soared after her song went viral online.
those: used to refer to people or things further away or already mentioned
Those houses on the hill were built a century ago.
shows: makes clear or proves that something is true
The evidence shows a clear link between smoking and lung disease.
another: one more, or a different one, of the same kind
Could I have another cup of coffee, please?
looking: He spent the afternoon looking for his missing keys.
ahead: in a forward direction; in advance
The team stayed one point ahead until the final minute.
gives: The charity gives food and shelter to homeless families.
hope: a feeling of expectation or desire for something to happen
She never lost hope that things would improve.
advice: guidance or recommendations offered about future action
Her grandmother's advice on saving money still guides her today.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
offer: to present something for someone to accept or refuse
The bank offered him a loan with a low interest rate.
emerging: newly starting to appear, grow, or become important
Investors are watching several emerging technologies this year.
poets: Young poets gathered to share their work at the open mic.
seeking: trying to find or obtain something
People seeking better jobs often move to bigger cities.
own: to possess something, or belonging to oneself
Few families in the village own a car of their own.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
day: a period of twenty-four hours, or the time when it is light
She spent the whole day preparing for the interview.
utopia: an imagined place or state in which everything is perfect
The novel describes a utopia where poverty no longer exists.
stop: to come to an end or cause something to end
The bus will stop right outside the school gate.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
aimed: directed toward a particular goal or target
The new program is aimed at reducing traffic in the city center.
matter: a subject or situation being considered or discussed
Choosing the right career is a matter that deserves careful thought.
bizarre: It was a bizarre coincidence that both strangers wore identical jackets.
days: It took several days for the flood water to fully recede.
face: to be forced to deal with a difficult situation
Small businesses face rising costs again this year.
two: Two things mark it as worth keeping.
cents: small units of currency, or figuratively, a small opinion offered
He offered his two cents on how to fix the problem.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
classic: widely known and considered a typical example of its kind
The island's towers form a classic example of karst scenery.
nectar: a sweet liquid produced by flowers and collected by bees
Bees collect nectar from flowers to make honey.
philosophy: the study of fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, and values
She studied philosophy before becoming a full-time writer.
exists: A structure that already exists is easier to fill than one built from nothing.
travel: to go from one place to another, especially over a distance
observe: to watch someone or something carefully
Astronomers use powerful telescopes to observe distant galaxies.
immerse: involve someone deeply in an activity or surroundings
đắm mình, hòa mình (vào ngôn ngữ)
Students often immerse themselves in the culture to learn faster.
yourself: used to refer back to the person being spoken to
chính bạn, tự bản thân bạn
Testing yourself is slow, and every gap you find feels like a small failure.
stay: to continue to be in a place or condition
She decided to stay with the exercise plan for a full year.
calm: to become quieter, less intense, or less agitated
Traders hope the market will calm down after this week's volatility.
after: following in time or place; later than
The shop stays open late after the holiday season begins.
popular: liked, supported, or used by many people
That café became popular with students soon after it opened.
lose: to no longer have something; to be deprived of
If you lose your password, you can reset it online.
